content:
maria: Heads up — AcmePay reporting sustained latency spikes + intermittent 429s on dedicated pool eu-ded-04. Customer sees 10–20s tails and retry storms, started ~3139989600. Can someone pick this up?
ev an: @maria on it. pinging SREs. any quick metrics?
ops-bot: :warning: Alert: dedicated-pool eu-ded-04 throughput -62% at 3139989600. Autoscaler +1 node triggered; 4 requests rejected. dashboard: https://dash/internal/pools/eu-ded-04
sre-alex: Digging in — continuous-batcher queue depth spiked, avg batch size dropped from ~12 -> ~2 requests, token-per-batch also down. Lots of prefill=true requests in the trace. Looks like prefill-heavy traffic starving batcher coalescing.
ryan: That matches prior tenant pinball issues. If many short prefills hit the packer, microbatches shrink and throughput collapses. Check max_batch_tokens + batch_window + prefill_prioritization.
maria: Customer says these are short prompts but frequent multi-turn reruns + function-calls. They report billing anomalies (retries). I asked them to throttle but they can't fully.
ev an: Sharing quick repro I'm running: repeat 200 requests/sec with short prompts and prefills. curl example:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Customer-ID: acmepay" -d '\\"{\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"hi\\\", \\\"prefill\\\":true}\\"' &
done
```
sre-alex: Thanks. Quick mitigations to try: 1) increase batch_window from 8ms -> 20ms on pool eu-ded-04 to favor fill; 2) raise max_batch_tokens to 4096 for that pool; 3) temporarily route AcmePay to eu-ded-07 where batching is stable. Also check recent scheduler change that lowered packer aggressiveness (commit 7a4c2e1).
chris: Billing ops flagged a charge spike and paused invoice processing for AcmePay. They need exact request timestamps for 3139989500–3139990200 to reconcile. How to export?
ev an: export command:
```bash
./tools/query_logs --start 3139989500 --end 3139990200 --filter "customer:acmepay AND pool:eu-ded-04" > acmepay-31399895-31399902.log
```
maria: I'm going to roll a canary: bump batch_window to 20ms and enable aggressive prefix cache for pool eu-ded-04. Rolling now, will monitor for 10m.
ops-bot: Deploy started by maria to pool eu-ded-04. Canary id cny-2026-03-17-01.
sre-alex: If that doesn't recover, we should rollback scheduler commit 7a4c2e1 — hypothesis: that change biases toward micro-latency and starves packer. Also consider lowering prefill priority temporarily.
chris: Noted — billing will hold until we confirm retries stopped. Please paste the log export once ready.
maria: Update after 6m: avg batch size climbed back to ~9, P95/P99 latency dropped to baseline, 429s ceased. Customer confirms degraded UX resolved. We'll keep canary for 30m then promote.
sre-alex: Great. Post-action items: 1) add canary gating for scheduler packer changes; 2) create a safety config that increases batch_window automatically when avg batch size < 4 for >60s; 3) follow up with AcmePay to explain transient retries and confirm billing adjustments.
ev an: Filing support ticket to close loop with customer ops.
maria: Closing here. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
